Subject: Post-call: Redwood procurement path (PO vs Card / Marketplace)

Hi Lisa — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Key ask: Proof-of-concept to benchmark latency and cost on your typical transaction mix.
- Preferred product path: Hosted API for pilot, then Dedicated if predictable throughput required.
- Procurement questions we discussed: AP preference for PO vs card, vendor onboarding requirements, and potential marketplace purchase (AWS/GCP).

To move forward I can do one of the following based on what works best for your AP team: 
1) Pilot on credit card (no PO) if spend is expected to be < $5k/month — fastest path (we can limit consumption).
2) Pilot + Dedicated via PO/contract (if you want data isolation and higher throughput) — will require vendor registration + SOW.
3) Purchase via marketplace (AWS Marketplace) — can simplify procurement if your team prefers marketplace billing.

Attached: Redwood_Quote_v2.pdf (line-item pricing) and a short vendor onboarding checklist we use internally.

Next step: can you confirm which procurement path your AP prefers and any internal thresholds (card spend cap, vendor packet timeline)? If PO is required, please let us know the expected timeline for vendor onboarding and whether we should prepare a standard MSA/SOW.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement if helpful.






—Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood procurement path (PO vs Card / Marketplace)

Thanks Marissa — good notes. A few points from AP and procurement side: 

- AP policy: We generally require a PO for ongoing SaaS commitments over $5,000/month. For one-off or pilot spend below that threshold, we allow payment via corporate card.
- Vendor onboarding: required for any new vendor regardless of payment method. Typical items: W-9, vendor questionnaire, bank details, vendor registration form. Vendor onboarding usually takes 7–14 business days once we have completed paperwork.
- Marketplace: We prefer marketplace purchases when available since billing and invoicing are handled through AWS Marketplace, which often bypasses some internal vendor setup steps. However not all vendors are available there and some enterprise terms still require a PO.
- Contracting: If we go PO, procurement will need a standard MSA and an SOW with clear pricing and delivery milestones (pilot success criteria).

I can start the vendor packet prep if you send the required documents (W-9, vendor form, standard MSA). For the pilot, if you can guarantee we stay under the $5k/month threshold, the fastest path would be card. Otherwise we will need to open a vendor record and issue a PO.

I'll loop in procurement@finco.com for tracking.

Best,
Lisa Turner
Director, Strategic Partnerships — FinCo Payments

- I'll attach our vendor onboarding bundle (Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf) and the updated quote (Redwood_Quote_v2.pdf) — includes a monthly not-to-exceed option for the pilot so you can stay under the $5k cap if you prefer the card route.
- If you want us in the AWS Marketplace path, we can share the Marketplace SKU and pricing; note that Marketplace billing carries a separate terms flow and can be easier for AP but may affect contract term negotiation.
- If you choose PO: we'll prepare an MSA + SOW with pilot success criteria and pricing schedule; please advise the PO contact and any PO template to fill out.

Proposed timeline options: 
- Card pilot: start within 3 business days after card is provided and test data is ready.
- PO + onboarding: 10–14 business days to vendor active + SOW signature, then pilot start.
- Marketplace: dependent on your marketplace admin — typically 5–10 business days.

Quick note from our side on technical ops: 

- Dedicated deployment: requires a PO/contract since we provision reserved capacity; lead time depends on the instance size but plan for ~2 weeks after PO is active for full Dedicated provisioning.
- Hosted API pilot: perfectly fine to run on card and we can set hard consumption limits at the account level to keep spend under $5k/month.
- Marketplace deployments: for AWS Marketplace we can enable SSO and bill via Marketplace SKU, but there are additional steps for entitlement mapping — we can coordinate with your cloud procurement team if you go that route.

Happy to join a procurement call if you want a quick walkthrough of the ops and billing differences.


—Aditya
